clue.text: Flowers and fruit, the finest specimen

parts.note: flags are irises, flowers of riverbanks and ponds
a hip is the fruit of the wild rose

explanation.surface: A display of flowers and fruit judged the best example on show.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagship is the best or most important one of a group, by extension from a fleet's lead vessel.

clue.text: Part of Cockney's speech disheartened girl — total disaster to end

indicators.note: a word losing its heart keeps only its outside letters, here the first and last of girl
a disaster leaves things in ruins, so the letters of total are thrown into a new order

parts.note: to stop is to end something

explanation.surface: A heartbroken girl's total disaster finally comes to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' leaves GL from girl; 'disaster' makes OTTAL from total.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cockney typically replaces the t sound with a catch in the throat, a characteristic feature of that London accent.

clue.text: Men abhor artificial tree

indicators.note: artificial means made up, so these letters are manufactured into a different word

explanation.surface: Men loathe a fake tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'artificial' shuffles the letters of MEN ABHOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The hornbeam is a hardwood tree common in European woodland and hedges, an example of the defined class.

clue.text: Prospect of sudden death puts players on the spot

definitions.meaning: a football tiebreak that may go to sudden death, where one miss decides it
players take kicks from the penalty spot, and are under pressure

explanation.definitionFit: A football tiebreak of spot kicks ends in sudden death if level, with each player taking a kick from the penalty spot.

clue.text: Did author have power to stir from bed?

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics
to roust someone is to rouse them out of bed

explanation.surface: Did a writer ever manage to get himself out of bed?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to the novelist's famous habit of writing in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcel Proust was the French novelist who wrote In Search of Lost Time.

clue.text: Competitor's place goes to philosopher

parts.note: PL is the usual abbreviation for place, as in street names
A. J. Ayer was a British philosopher of logical positivism

explanation.surface: A sportsman's spot in the team is handed over to a thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is someone taking part in a game or contest, a competitor.

clue.text: Be obliged to read out letter

indicators.note: something read out is spoken, so the letter is heard rather than seen

parts.note: the letter here is O, whose spoken name is the sound needed

explanation.surface: Feeling duty-bound to read out a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To owe is to be in debt or under an obligation to someone.

clue.text: In school, an illegal occupation is a monster

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, so the school abbreviation wraps the rest

parts.note: an gives A, the indefinite article
a squat is a building occupied without legal right

explanation.surface: Squatters in a school building are a terrible thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the container signal: the school abbreviation is split as S...CH to hold the rest. 'Illegal occupation' sounds like a crime, but it is just squatting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sasquatch, or Bigfoot, is a legendary ape-like monster of North American forests.

clue.text: At centre for divorce, I run into a film maker

parts.note: Reno, Nevada, was famous for its quick divorces
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Heading to a divorce hub, I bump into a movie director.
explanation.walkthrough: Reno in Nevada was long known as the place Americans went for a quick divorce.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Renoir was a celebrated French film director, son of the painter.

clue.text: Allies initially found among most close group of countries

indicators.note: one letter is placed in the middle of the other word, found among its letters

parts.note: nearest means closest, most close

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Allies are first located among the closest bunch of nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes A from Allies, and 'found among' puts it inside NEAREST.
explanation.definitionFit: The Near East is an old name for the region of countries of south-west Asia and nearby.

clue.text: Model aeroplane's last to turn and *. land in the river

indicators.note: turning the run of letters round means it is read backwards

parts.note: a model, such as a model aeroplane, is a toy

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of aeroplane

explanation.surface: A model plane comes round and lands in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' reverses TOY plus E (the end of aeroplane), giving the letters back to front. The '*.' in the held clue is OCR noise and supplies nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyot, or ait, is a small island in a river, especially the Thames.

clue.text: William, do read out love letter.

indicators.note: read out means spoken, so what is heard counts, not the spelling

parts.note: William is nicknamed Billy, and do follows it, together sounding like the French phrase

explanation.surface: William is asked to read a romantic letter aloud to the room.
explanation.walkthrough: Billet-doux is French for 'sweet note' and is pronounced roughly 'billy doo'.
explanation.definitionFit: A billet-doux is a love letter, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Women's branch died out around one county

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the other pieces, enclosing them
out suggests disorder, so the letters of died are rearranged

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
Staffs is the abbreviation for Staffordshire, an English county

explanation.surface: A women's group has died out across one English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges died as DIDE, and 'around' splits it to hold the rest. Staffordshire is a county in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The distaff side of a family is the female line, the distaff being a spinning tool linked with women's work.

clue.text: Very awkward to include line by parent in prayer

indicators.note: one word takes in the others, including them within it

parts.note: hairy is slang for very tricky or awkward
ma is a familiar word for mother, a parent

explanation.surface: It's very tricky to fit a line by your mother into your prayers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' is the container signal; 'by' only places the line beside the parent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hail Mary is a Catholic prayer addressed to the Virgin Mary.

clue.text: Desperately plan plea at back of court? He may

definitions.text: Desperately plan plea at back of court? He may

indicators.note: desperately suggests frantic disorder, so these letters are rearranged
the back of a word is its final letter, here of court

explanation.surface: A litigant frantically draws up a plea at the rear of the courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desperately' rearranges PLAN PLEA; 'at back of' takes T from court. The whole clue describes the person.
explanation.definitionFit: An appellant is a person who appeals a court ruling, and would plan a plea to a higher court.

clue.text: Block a burrow

definitions.meaning: a squared paving stone used in roads is a block
a badger's home is a burrow underground

explanation.definitionFit: A sett is both a granite paving block and the burrow of a badger.

clue.text: Gone sick, taking drug —- in this form?

definitions.text: Gone sick, taking drug —- in this form?

parts.note: past means gone by
ill means sick
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Feeling ill and taking medicine, perhaps as a lozenge?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue suggests the medicine taken could come as a lozenge.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastille is a small medicated sweet, a form in which a sick person might take medicine.

clue.text: Caps put back in place

indicators.note: put back means turned round, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: tops are caps, as on bottles

explanation.surface: Lids are returned to where they belong.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a particular place or location.

clue.text: Brave choice of subject for Longfellow

definitions.meaning: a brave is a Native American warrior
Longfellow wrote a famous long poem about this hero

explanation.definitionFit: Hiawatha is the Native American hero of Longfellow's poem The Song of Hiawatha.

clue.text: If flood returns, one might need this for east coast port

definitions.text: If flood returns, one might need this
definitions.meaning: a second great flood would call for a fresh vessel like Noah's
a port city on the US east coast, in New Jersey

explanation.definitionFit: Newark is a New Jersey port city, and split up it is a new ark for another flood.

clue.text: Exhausted, cheered to the door?

definitions.meaning: worn out and finished, especially of a machine
applauded all the way out of a room

explanation.definitionFit: Clapped-out is British slang for worn out, and literally means applauded on the way out.

clue.text: Don't eat so quickly

explanation.definitionFit: To fast is to abstain from food, and fast also means quickly.

clue.text: At end of nuptials, shower with grain

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, here of nuptials

parts.note: to pelt is to shower with missiles, as guests shower a couple

explanation.surface: After a wedding, the couple are showered with rice.
explanation.definitionFit: Spelt is an ancient variety of wheat, a cereal grain.

clue.text: Sacked man going to depart, but I intervened — capital!

indicators.note: to intervene is to come between, so one letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: Santa is the man who carries a sack of presents
go means depart

explanation.surface: A fired man was about to leave, but I stepped in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacked' looks like fired; it is Santa's sack. 'intervened' puts I inside SANTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Santiago is the capital city of Chile.

clue.text: Tense before finishing letter from foreigner

indicators.note: stopping before the finish means dropping the final letter

parts.note: taut means tense, stretched tight

explanation.surface: A tense foreign correspondent writes before signing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before finishing' cuts the final T from TAUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tau is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so a letter from foreign writing.

clue.text: Lion at first paraded, then put in den

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of lion

parts.note: aired means shown off in public, paraded

explanation.surface: A lion is shown off, then shut up in its cage.
explanation.definitionFit: Laired means lodged in a lair, an animal's den.

clue.text: Hit in crowd by stone

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight
a ruck is a crowd or throng

explanation.surface: Someone in a crowd was hit by a thrown stone.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of weight of 14 pounds, abbreviated st.
explanation.definitionFit: Struck is the past tense of strike, meaning hit.

clue.text: Time to collect new and old artistic period

indicators.note: the outer letters gather up the middle word, collecting it between them

parts.note: recent means new

explanation.surface: Time to gather the new and the old for an art exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to collect' puts RECENT between T and O.
explanation.definitionFit: The trecento is the fourteenth century in Italian art and literature, the period of Giotto.
